key_insight: Adding a mediation mechanism on top of open communication is enough to keep self-interested agents trading productively, even under sustained adversarial trolling.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a practical design pattern for resilient multi-agent systems: layer formal conflict-resolution protocols to preserve utility and market stability under attack.
method: Simulated a marketplace with 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents with complementary production roles trading over a constrained social network.
Compared eight governance mechanisms across 200 rounds while progressively injecting trolls.
Red-teamed the best mechanism with iteratively prompt-optimized LLM trolls to test adversarial robustness.
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s evaluation, Mediation performed best in the mechanism comparison, and the strongest attack (v6) reduced honest-agent utility by 13.3% but did not collapse the market.
watch_item: Results come from a simulated 18-agent marketplace with one model family, so robustness may not fully transfer to larger, heterogeneous, or real-world human-agent settings.
paper_title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
